Per-cycle sequence quality profile

Source: R/mp_qc.R
mp_qc_profile.Rd

Draws the read-quality profile across sequencing cycles for one or more FASTQ files – the diagnostic used to choose DADA2/QIIME 2 truncation lengths. For each cycle (base position) it shows the distribution of Phred quality scores as a frequency heatmap ("heatmap"), or the per-cycle mean with an inter-quartile ribbon ("line"), overlaid with mean / quartile summary lines. A horizontal reference line marks a target quality (Q30 by default).

Usage

mp_qc_profile(
  x,
  aggregate = FALSE,
  n = 5e+05,
  sample.names = NULL,
  plot.type = c("heatmap", "line"),
  show = c("mean", "quartiles"),
  quality.line = 30,
  palette = NULL,
  theme = NULL,
  ...,
  plot.title = NULL,
  plot.subtitle = NULL,
  plot.caption = NULL,
  font.size = getOption("micropubr.font.size", 11),
  interactive = FALSE,
  return.data = FALSE,
  verbose = getOption("micropubr.verbose", FALSE)
)

Arguments

x

A character vector of FASTQ file paths (wildcards allowed), a single directory containing FASTQ files, or a per-cycle quality data frame (file, cycle, score, count).

aggregate

Pool all files into a single combined profile.

n

Maximum number of reads to sample per file when reading FASTQ.

sample.names

Optional display names, one per file (defaults to the file names with the FASTQ extension stripped).

plot.type

"heatmap" (per-cycle score frequencies) or "line" (mean with an inter-quartile ribbon).

show

Summary overlays to draw: any of "mean" and "quartiles".

quality.line

Phred score for the horizontal reference line (e.g. 30); NULL to omit it.

palette, theme, plot.title, plot.subtitle, plot.caption, font.size

See mp_alpha().

...

Passed to the primary geom.

interactive

If TRUE, return an interactive plotly widget instead of a static ggplot (requires plotly). See mp_alpha().

return.data

If TRUE, return the tidy per-cycle quality data frame (file, cycle, score, count) instead of a plot.

verbose

Print the methods used.

Value

A ggplot object; a plotly widget when interactive = TRUE; or a data frame when return.data = TRUE.

Details

Input can be FASTQ file paths (optionally .gz), a directory of FASTQ files, or a pre-computed per-cycle data frame with columns file, cycle, score and count (the shape returned by return.data = TRUE), so a summary can be saved once and re-plotted without re-reading the reads. Reading FASTQ files requires the ShortRead package.

See also

mp_import_dada2() for turning denoised reads into a phyloseq object once truncation lengths are chosen.

Examples

# Usually you pass FASTQ paths, e.g.
#   mp_qc_profile(c("sampleA_R1.fastq.gz", "sampleA_R2.fastq.gz"))
# which needs the 'ShortRead' package. Here we build an equivalent per-cycle
# summary by hand so the example runs anywhere:
set.seed(1)
grid <- expand.grid(file = c("R1.fastq.gz", "R2.fastq.gz"),
                    cycle = 1:120, score = 2:40)
mu <- 38 - 0.06 * grid$cycle - ifelse(grid$file == "R2.fastq.gz", 5, 0)
grid$count <- round(3000 * stats::dnorm(grid$score, mu, 2.5))
mp_qc_profile(grid[grid$count > 0, ])
